svg.text: Who fires what, where it is delivered, who reacts — with core/GUI territories and known hazards · org.omegat.core.CoreEvents · July 2026
Event catalogue — CoreEvents fire methods, listener interfaces, typical consumers

g.text: fireApplicationStartup / fireApplicationShutdown → IApplicationEventListener — plugin bootstrap and teardown
fireEntryNewFile / fireEntryActivated → IEntryEventListener — matches, glossary, dictionaries, MT, segment properties
fireFontChanged → IFontChangedEventListener — editor and panes re-apply the display font
fireEditorNewWord → IEditorEventListener — reacts to a newly typed word (e.g. event scripts)

svg.text: ⇠ core | GUI ⇢ EDT boundary — cross only via invokeLater / SwingWorker
FindMatchesThread — fuzzy search off the EDT
results → EDT: MatchesTextArea shows best matches
fire* never blocks — COMPILE listeners and their scripts may still be running while the commit proceeds (SF-1277)

g.text: • Every fire* method wraps delivery in SwingUtilities.invokeLater — listeners always run on the EDT, and the caller never waits for them.
• Listeners run in registration order; each call is individually try/catch-ed and logged (ERROR_EVENT_…), so one broken listener cannot break the loop.
• Components and plugins subscribe statically: CoreEvents.register…Listener(…) / unregister…Listener(…) — from anywhere, at any time.
• Rule of thumb: react quickly on the EDT and push long work to a SwingWorker — the matcher, the event scripts and the MT connectors all do exactly that.

APPLICATION_STARTUP fires before most listeners could register (startup scripts run from ScriptsMonitor.start() instead); SHUTDOWN scripts may be cut off — the JVM can exit first (FIXME in ScriptsMonitor).
CoreEvents is a static, mutable singleton bus: hidden coupling between components, registration-order sensitivity, and tests need TestCoreInitializer scaffolding.
Anything slow inside a listener freezes the whole UI — the EDT is the application's single UI thread. Long work must go to a SwingWorker.

Several panes read colours and fonts only once at construction (MatchesTextArea even caches attribute sets statically) — live updates need an explicit broadcast: fonts have fireFontChanged; colours have no equivalent broadcast yet.
fireProjectChange(COMPILE) is fire-and-forget: committing target files can overtake compile-time event scripts that still modify them (SF-1277).
